AP: Mexico to request criminal charges over deaths following fatal shooting of Houston man by ICE agents
July 9, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Mexico will seek charges over 17 citizens dead in ICE custody or operations — but AP leads its account of the Houston killing with DHS's claim the man "attempted to ram an agent," and notes the request "carries no legal weight." 🔍

14 died in ICE custody, 3 during ICE operations. Salgado Araujo had lived in the US for decades and was driving a work crew to a construction site when he was shot.

• Sheinbaum: "We are going to do everything in our power, because we cannot stand silent"
• the deaths of Mexicans "whose only crime is working honestly in the United States"

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO'S SOCIAL SPENDING SURGES: EDUCATION +21%, HEALTH +20.9% REAL IN 2026</u>

SHCP's public-finance report shows that from January to May 2026, real annual spending rose +21% on education and +20.9% on health, with overall social-development spending up 13.1% — above the last decade's average, per El Economista. Health investment tripled in real terms versus 2025 — all while inflation sits at a 5-year low (3.37% in June).

🇲🇽🌽 <u>4 BILLION PESOS FOR THE P'URHÉPECHA PEOPLE — HEALTH, SCHOOLS, ROADS, WATER</u>

One year and two months into the Plan de Justicia for the P'urhépecha people of Michoacán, President Sheinbaum reported over 4 billion pesos invested across 146 communities: 646 doctors and more than 1,000 nurses hired, a new ISSSTE hospital, and 27 community-built "artisanal roads" (485 million pesos) — plus schools, water, housing, farm support and the recovery of Paracho's guitar-making tradition, decided with the pueblos, not for them.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO'S MET SERVICE FORECASTS A "VERY STRONG" EL NIÑO INTO 2027</u>

Mexico's Servicio Meteorológico Nacional puts the odds of El Niño forming at 97–100%, with a 63% chance it reaches "very strong" — on par with the 1997-98 and 2015-16 events — peaking November 2026 to January 2027. Sea-surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region have already hit 29.2°C, just 0.2° below the November 2015 record. Expect rainfall deficits across central, southern and southeastern Mexico this summer, then a wetter, colder northern winter. "The trend is consistent with a very strong forming El Niño," the SMN coordinator said.

🇲🇽🐝 <u>MEXICO'S SUPREME COURT TAKES UP CASE TO RECOGNIZE BEES AS SUBJECTS OF RIGHTS</u>

The SCJN voted to hear a landmark case brought by Maya communities of Hopelchén, Campeche, seeking legal recognition of the melipona bee as a subject of rights — after documenting mass die-offs tied to pesticides like fipronil and neonicotinoids. Minister Guerrero García said the ruling could "set criteria recognizing the melipona bee as a legal subject of protection" and force new rules on aerial and drone fumigation. The Court also took up cases on the Ring of Cenotes reserve and the limits of industrial pig farming on Indigenous land.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US DEMANDED MEXICO KEEP EXTRADITION CASE SECRET — THEN EXPOSED IT ITSELF</u>

On President Sheinbaum's orders, the Foreign Ministry released documents on the US extradition requests against Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and nine other officials. One revelation: Washington asked Mexico to keep the arrest requests confidential — then, the very next day, the Southern District of New York publicly announced the charges and names itself (official document dated April 30). The ten face conspiracy-to-import-fentanyl charges; any action, Mexico stresses, depends on the evidence the FGR actually presents.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US WEAPONIZES NARCO ACCUSATIONS TO WEAKEN GOVERNMENTS — SHEINBAUM</u>

President Sheinbaum says Washington has repeatedly used accusations of "narco ties" against politicians to interfere with and weaken governments — not only hers, but AMLO's before her. "The United States has sought to have interference... when we have a bilateral extradition treaty that is always valued by Mexico," she said, recalling Iran-Contra, where Washington itself used cartels to move weapons and topple a regime. Mexico will keep cooperating against trafficking, she added — but asked the US to finally investigate how the drugs get in, where they're sold, and where the money is laundered.

🇲🇽📉 <u>MEXICO'S INFLATION KEEPS FALLING — PRODUCER PRICES CRASH ON CHEAP OIL</u>

Producer inflation (INPP) dropped to 2.10% annually in June, down from 2.93% in May, dragged lower by a 20% monthly plunge in crude and an 8.5% drop in gasoline, per INEGI. Consumer inflation landed at 3.37% — the lowest in over five years and inside Banxico's target band for a second straight month, helped by cheaper tomatoes, lemons and chiles. The "uncertainty" the IMF keeps warning about isn't showing up in the price data.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO BETS ON TECH SOVEREIGNTY: OWN CAR, OWN CHIPS, OWN SATELLITE</u>

Secihti presented 13 strategic projects to build Mexican technological independence: the Olinia — a 100% Mexican-designed electric car headed for mass production in 2027 — the Kutsari semiconductor design workshop, a national satellite, drones, and a Pacific climate-monitoring system, plus a homegrown framework to regulate AI. "Technological independence and our own knowledge," in the words of Secihti head Rosaura Ruiz. Sovereignty isn't just oil and borders anymore — it's chips and code too.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICAN LAW ALREADY REQUIRES MEDIA TO HAVE ETHICS. MOST IGNORE IT.</u>

Interior Secretary Luisa María Alcalde reminded the press that outlets are legally obligated to maintain codes of ethics, appoint audience ombudsmen, and verify what they publish — pointing to a fabricated interview run by El Universal as exhibit A. The same outlets that manufacture "narco-state" headlines for foreign consumption can't be bothered to check a quote at home. Accountability isn't censorship; it's the bare minimum they demand of everyone but themselves.
